comments: Nanaka's being quite inaccurate here. "一時キャッシュ" is the temporary cache... of an Internet browser. If that cache gets corrupted, then you gotta clear it, not reset the PC; then again, that's the whole point, isn't it? It works exactly like this in the time loop: he clears the RAM over and over, but the content of the hokora ain't gonna change. -GHS

adjudicated.remedy: Use “Even Wi***ws can repeat the same error after you think you’ve reset it, because of the temporary cache.”

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I will, I will, come in and I will!"

adjudicated.jp: 背後にまわって下着を見ようとする俺。
adjudicated.en: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he moves around behind her to look at her underwear. “Turning to my back” reverses the direction, and “go I” is malformed inversion.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I circled around behind her to look at her underwear.”

highlights.text: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.

adjudicated.jp: ノーコンのブルマだった。
adjudicated.en:
Buruma Out of Control*.
* Dark blue
comments: http://detail.chiebukuro.yahoo.co.jp/qa/question_detail/q1259121567 (J only), basically no control means dark blue, so going with cryptic and silly because that's actually literal. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source identifies the bloomers’ dark navy color. “Out of Control” invents a meaning for ノーコン, while the footnote only partially repairs the mistranslation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “They were dark navy bloomers.”

adjudicated.jp: 女性解放運動も真っ青なセクハラ体操着としてずいぶん前に絶滅したという、ブルマ！？
adjudicated.en: That deep blue gym sexual harassment-ish uniform hunted down to extinction a fair while ago by the women's lib movement, that is, buruma?!
comments: According to Wikipedia it's a "mid-90s" thing indeed, so he's just after them. -GHS

adjudicated.remedy: Use “Bloomers—the harassing gymwear, enough to make even the women’s liberation movement blanch, said to have gone extinct long ago!?”

adjudicated.jp: 俺はわなわなと震えた。
adjudicated.en: I shook and trembled with fear.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he trembles violently; it does not specify fear. The surrounding reaction may instead be shock or excitement.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “I trembled violently.”

adjudicated.jp: 噂によれば、そのヒップへの張りつき具合は絶品だと言う。
adjudicated.en: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.
comments: Hmmm, but he talks as if he didn't collect buruma... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rumor praises how exquisitely the bloomers cling to the hips. The English calls the object itself “a superlative article” and loses the quality of the fit.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Rumor says the way they cling to the hips is exquisite.”

highlights.text: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.

adjudicated.jp: 「アンテナ、ちゃっちゃっと組み立てちゃいなさいよね」
adjudicated.en: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source tells him to assemble the antenna briskly. “Pretty and fast” treats ちゃっちゃっと as two separate qualities.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Put that antenna together, and make it quick.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"

adjudicated.jp: チェーンが小気味よい音をたてて、まわる。
adjudicated.en: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.
adjudicated.assessment: The singular subject “chain” requires “spins.”
adjudicated.remedy: Use “The chain spins with a crisp, pleasant sound.”

highlights.text: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.

adjudicated.jp: タイヤがアスファルトを擦り、自転車が走り出す。
adjudicated.en: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.
adjudicated.assessment: The singular “tire” requires “grazes,” and a bicycle itself begins to move or roll rather than “ride forth.”
adjudicated.remedy: Use “The tire grazes the asphalt, and the bicycle rolls away.”

highlights.text: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.

withheld.jp: 要するに王道に対して常に皮相的な立場を保つって行為は自己顕示欲に支配された瞬間に堕するってことだよね」
withheld.en: Taichi: "The point is that acting in constant preservation of superficial positions is the easy way, and it's destined to degenerate into moments dominated by conspicuous exhibitionism."
comments: Hooo man this barely makes any sense. Best I can tell "don't just be bland, 'cause then you'll go blandly super-extraordinary with nothing 'real' in between", i.e. no superficial twists of the kind Cross Channel is unfortunately believed to be the king of. This is where the criticism of characterization and balancing meets the Inevitability of Downfall theme. ...and there goes another sentence I thought I'd never write in my life. See CCC0045A, "don't hope to revolutionize things with little tweaks", similar(?) but clearer(???). -GHS
